description: Pipeline StepMiddleware lifecycle (Issue #33): before_step / after_step / on_step_error invocation order, recovery semantics, error propagation, and async support. The callbacks are before_step(step_name, state), after_step(step_name, state, result), on_step_error(step_name, state, error) — all three SDKs agree, and `state` is the PipelineState view. There is NO step-inputs parameter: a Step is execute(ctx), so nothing exists for a middleware to replace. References features/middleware-system.md 'Pipeline Step Middleware'.

test_cases.description: before_step runs in registration order; after_step runs in reverse registration order (onion model)
First on_step_error handler returning a non-null value provides recovery and short-circuits remaining handlers; the original error MUST NOT propagate
When all on_step_error handlers return null/None, the original error MUST continue propagating (subject to ignore_errors)
If before_step of mw_b raises, on_step_error MUST be invoked only on mw_b (and earlier executed mws), reverse order; mw_c (not yet executed) MUST NOT be invoked

Async StepMiddleware callbacks MUST be awaited before the pipeline advances: the coroutine/Promise/Future MUST be resolved, not merely created and dropped. The previous revision asserted the step observed a value returned by an async before_step. There is no step-inputs parameter, so the only observable proof of awaiting is that the side effect landed before the pipeline moved on.

before_step returning a value MUST NOT change what the step body sees. The hook observes; it does not rewrite. This is the inverse of the removed `before_step_input_replacement` case, kept so the mistaken contract cannot quietly return.

A before_step failure terminates the step and is NOT recoverable. on_step_error is still invoked on the already-executed middlewares — for observation and cleanup only — and any value it returns MUST be discarded: it MUST NOT become the step's output and MUST NOT let the pipeline continue. Honouring it would advance past a step whose body never ran, and the built-in strategy puts acl_check and approval_gate in that sequence, so it is an authorization bypass reachable from an extension point that carries no authority.

A step body that failed and was recovered by on_step_error produced an output and the pipeline continued, so the onion MUST close: after_step runs, in reverse registration order. A middleware that acquired something in before_step must get its after_step or the recovery path leaks. This is the STEP-BODY failure path and is deliberately the opposite of `before_step_failure_recovery_is_discarded`. Also pins `state.outputs` on the RECOVERY path: a recovered step is still the current step, so `after_step` MUST NOT see it. That ordering lives at a SECOND snapshot site in each engine, and `state_outputs_excludes_the_current_step_in_every_hook` cannot reach it — it recovers from nothing. Swapping the two lines at the recovery site left every conformance case green in apcore-typescript until this expectation was added.

`state.outputs` contains exactly the steps that completed BEFORE the current one — never the current step, in any hook. The alternative reading, 'outputs of completed steps', would make after_step the one hook whose outputs differs in shape, so a middleware would have to know which hook it was in before reading the map. The current step's output reaches after_step as the `result` parameter; carrying the same value down two paths is how the two drift apart.

driver_contract.no_input_replacement: before_step is an OBSERVATION hook; its return value carries no meaning. An earlier revision of this fixture asserted that a returned dict replaced the step's inputs — a calling convention that exists in no SDK, because Step.execute takes only ctx.
driver_contract.step_names_are_real: Built-in steps are context_creation, call_chain_guard, module_lookup, acl_check, approval_gate, middleware_before, input_validation, execute, output_validation, middleware_after, return_result. An earlier revision used `validate_input`, which is not one of them.
driver_contract.order_is_the_assertion: after_step and on_step_error run in REVERSE registration order (onion model). Asserting only the SET of invoked middlewares passes against a straight-through implementation and is the single most common way this fixture is driven vacuously — assert the ordered list.
driver_contract.first_recovery_wins: The first on_step_error returning a non-null value supplies the recovery result and short-circuits the remaining handlers. An implementation that runs all handlers and keeps the LAST non-null return produces the same value whenever only one handler recovers, so the recovery case MUST have two handlers that both would recover.
driver_contract.assert_the_wire_code: Every error expectation is a WIRE CODE (`wrapper_error_code`, `original_error_code`), never a class name. An earlier revision of THIS fixture — written in the same sweep that filed the issue against class-name assertions — used `wrapped_in: "MiddlewareChainError"` / "PipelineStepError". Those are Python/TypeScript class names; apcore-rust has neither type, only `ErrorCode` variants, so no Rust driver could assert them. apcore-python's driver "checked" the key by comparing the fixture to a string literal — a tautology that cannot fail on SDK behaviour — and the TS and Rust drivers ignored it entirely. The codes are MIDDLEWARE_CHAIN_ERROR and PIPELINE_STEP_ERROR in all three SDKs.
driver_contract.wrapper_is_load_bearing: Drivers MUST assert `wrapper_error_code`. Removing the MiddlewareChainError wrapping from an SDK was verified to leave every driver GREEN before this was pinned — in apcore-typescript and apcore-rust alike. It is the single behaviour the before_step fix exists to provide.
driver_contract.step_output_is_a_MUST: `on_step_error_recovery_short_circuits.expected.step_output` pins the rule that the recovery value BECOMES the step's output (features/middleware-system.md, Normative Rules). All three SDKs now do this. apcore-typescript previously declined on purpose (src/pipeline.ts: "the recovery value is informational ... NOT auto-merged into ctx.output") and the field was asserted by apcore-python's driver alone, so a MUST was being violated in the open. Drivers MUST assert it.
driver_contract.before_step_failure_is_terminal: A before_step failure and a step-body failure MUST NOT share a recovery path. On the before_step path the recovery value is DISCARDED, after_step does NOT fire, and the step's `ignore_errors` does NOT apply — `MiddlewareChainError` propagates regardless. Drivers MUST assert `recovery_honored: false` by observing that the FOLLOWING step did not execute, not merely that an error was raised: an implementation that honours the recovery and then happens to fail later would satisfy a raise-only assertion while the bypass is live.
driver_contract.two_recovery_paths: `before_step_failure_recovery_is_discarded` and `after_step_fires_after_a_recovered_step` are deliberate opposites. Both had TWO middlewares returning a recovery so that first-wins is distinguishable, and both use a real built-in step name — `acl_check` in the first, because the rule exists to protect the gates.
driver_contract.cleanup_pass_does_not_short_circuit: In `before_step_failure_recovery_is_discarded`, `on_step_error_invoked` is ["mw_b", "mw_a"] while mw_b RETURNS a recovery value. That is deliberate: first-recovery-wins is for shopping for a recovery, and this pass is not shopping — every already-entered middleware MUST be notified so it can clean up. An implementation that reuses its normal on_step_error helper here will short-circuit at mw_b and strand mw_a; the expectation is written to catch exactly that.
driver_contract.assert_the_exact_key_set: Drivers MUST assert the EXACT key set of `state.outputs`, not that a particular key is absent. `assert 'second' not in outputs` also passes against an implementation that lost `first`, and against one that never populated the map at all. The three expectations differ from each other on purpose: `on_step_error` is observed on the THIRD step, so it proves the map does keep earlier steps while excluding the failing one — an all-empty map would satisfy the other two.
driver_contract.outputs_is_a_live_reference: `state.outputs` is a LIVE reference to the engine's map in at least apcore-typescript, not a copy. A driver that stashes the reference and reads it after `run()` returns sees the FINAL map on every entry and can never fail. Snapshot the key set INSIDE the hook.
driver_contract.both_snapshot_sites: Each engine snapshots `step_outputs` at TWO sites — after the natural success path and after the recovery path — and only the first is reachable from `state_outputs_excludes_the_current_step_in_every_hook`. `after_step_fires_after_a_recovered_step` carries the second. Drivers MUST assert both, or half the rule is unpinned.
